slides.heading: Reception — Spring 2, Week 4
slides.sub: New sounds taught directly, practised and applied in words, captions and the matching decodable book.

slides.heading: Mon
slides.objective: Learn the new sound "air" (/eə/) and start reading and spelling words that use it.

slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="chair" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="chair_air"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.mnemonic: Amara the feather drifts on the breeze, floating and swaying, air-air, before it lands.

character.name: Amara
character.blurb: Amara is a light feather who never falls straight down — she always drifts and sways on the air first.

slides.pronunciation_note: A gliding sound, 'air' as in 'chair' — start open and glide gently towards 'uh', let your voice float.
slides.formation_cue: Write 'a', then 'i', then 'r', close together — three letters, one sound.
slides.action: Hold one hand up like a feather and let it drift side to side slowly through the air, saying air-air.
slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="chair" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="chair_air"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.tip: The letters don't sound out the way you'd expect for a short word — it rhymes with 'car' and 'star', so borrow that 'ar' sound to help remember it.

slides.dictation: A chair has a pair of legs.

slides.heading: Tue
slides.objective: Learn the new sound "ure" (/ʊə/) and start reading and spelling words that use it.

slides.mnemonic: Ursa the snail tucks in sure and steady, ure-ure, whenever her shell feels safe and snug.

character.name: Ursa
character.blurb: Ursa only ever moves when she's sure it's safe, tucking snug into her shell with a soft ure-ure hum.

slides.pronunciation_note: A gliding sound, 'ure' as in 'sure' — lips rounded to start, gliding gently towards 'uh', soft and short.
slides.formation_cue: Write 'u', then 'r', then 'e', close together — three letters, one sound.
slides.action: Wrap your arms around yourself in a snug hug and hum ure-ure.

slides.heading: Wed
slides.objective: Learn the new sound "er" (/ə/) and start reading and spelling words that use it.

slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="hammer" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="hammer"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.mnemonic: Ember the mushroom mutters a soft, quiet er-er whenever a raindrop taps her cap.

character.name: Ember
character.blurb: Ember is a quiet mushroom who only ever mutters her sound softly, never loudly, whenever it rains.

slides.pronunciation_note: 'er' as in 'her' and 'fern' — a steady sound like 'ur'. At the end of a longer word, as in 'hammer', it is lighter and quicker.
slides.formation_cue: Write 'e', then 'r', close together — two letters, one sound.
slides.action: Shrug your shoulders lightly and mutter a soft, quick er-er.
slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="hammer" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="hammer"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.dictation: The herd is on the farm.

slides.heading: Thu
slides.objective: Extra practice blending and segmenting everything taught this week — no new content today.

slides.heading: Fri
slides.objective: Revisit everything taught this week, read the matched decodable book, and check how securely it has been learned.
